clue.text: Kids power fairly distributed for light diversion

indicators.note: letters spread about and dealt out afresh are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Children's energy is shared out evenly in return for some light entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges all fifteen letters of KIDS POWER FAIRLY; 'light diversion' is literal, an entertainment made of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyrotechnic show is entertainment made of light, so it is literally a light diversion.

clue.text: Doubles as chef set for sack

indicators.note: to sack a town is to wreck it, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's set of tools is offered as two portions in exchange for a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' wreaks havoc on CHEF SET, rearranging it. Doubles here are ghostly lookalikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetch is an apparition of a living person, a ghostly double or wraith.

clue.text: What's left of old house for bankrupts

definitions.meaning: the crumbling remains of an ancient building
brings someone to financial collapse, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Ruins are the remains of a building, and to ruin someone is to bankrupt them.

clue.text: Standard opening gambit in peace talks?

definitions.text: Standard opening gambit in peace talks?

parts.words: Standard opening gambit in peace talks
parts.note: a standard is a banner, and the first move towards a truce is raising a banner of surrender

explanation.definitionFit: Waving a pale banner signals surrender or truce, the flag that opens negotiations.

clue.text: Manage unbroken rampage

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a horse that has not been broken in is wild

explanation.surface: Someone controls an untamed horse on a violent spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to behave without restraint, a phrasal synonym for going out of control.

clue.text: Disasters caused by surges of current in the mains?

definitions.text: Disasters caused by surges of current in the mains?

parts.words: Disasters caused by surges of current in the mains
parts.note: reads like electrical power surges, but the main is the sea and the current is water

explanation.definitionFit: Floods are disasters of water overwhelming land, often from surges of the sea, poetically the main.

clue.text: Rascal given quarter on military base

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it

parts.note: S for south is one quarter of the compass
a camp is a base for soldiers

explanation.surface: A rogue is billeted in lodgings at an army base.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rogue, a synonym for rascal.

clue.text: The declension of "Terra"?

parts.note: looks like Latin grammar, but read as the earth (Latin terra) declining or sliding down

explanation.definitionFit: A mass of earth slipping down a slope is a fall of land, here a punning decline of earth.

clue.text: Delivered by cricketer to royal house-the Queen's

parts.note: the House of York was an English royal dynasty
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A cricketer hands something over to the palace belonging to Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batter's feet, so these are things a bowler delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkers are a kind of cricket ball bowled to land at the batter's toes, deliveries by a bowler.

clue.text: A giver of knowledge turning out in it…

indicators.note: turning the letters about rearranges them into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher is coming out from within something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges OUT IN IT. The clue runs on into the next one with its trailing dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching or instruction is what imparts knowledge to students.

clue.text: … with quid breadwinner in the class

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, and a quid is British slang for a pound
the person who earns the household's income is its earner

explanation.surface: Someone bringing home a pound is a member of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is everyday British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is someone in the class, receiving lessons from a teacher.

clue.text: Giving your own feet a good lick?

definitions.text: Giving your own feet a good lick?

parts.words: Giving your own feet a good lick
parts.note: suggests licking one's feet, but a good lick is a fast pace, so this is speeding along

explanation.definitionFit: Going at a good lick means moving quickly, so hurrying your feet is a form of speeding up.

clue.text: Its sticky tape's run out!

indicators.note: when the tape runs out its letters spill loose and are rearranged

parts.note: tape's is read as tape is, keeping the S

explanation.surface: A complaint that the adhesive roll has been used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' rearranges TAPES; the whole clue also describes an adhesive that takes over when tape is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a sticky adhesive used for fixing paper, much like tape.

clue.text: Paid for a seat with a penny

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench seat with a high back
D stood for penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone bought a chair for one penny.
explanation.walkthrough: D (from Latin denarius) was the old British penny symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill is to pay it, so a settled account has been paid.

clue.text: Fringe part of pot plants?

parts.note: sounds like horticulture, but the pot is a teapot and fringe refers to fortune-telling from what is left in it

explanation.definitionFit: The dried foliage of a tea shrub goes in the pot, and its dregs are read in fringe divination.

clue.text: Distress that's characteristic on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts something inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is aboard
a trait is a characteristic feature

explanation.surface: Suffering that is typical aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' does double duty in the surface: being on board a ship means being inside the steamship abbreviation, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in dire straits means being in great difficulty, so the plural noun carries the sense of distress.

clue.text: Peculiar old policeman gets drink smuggler

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
the Bow Street Runners were an early London police force

explanation.surface: A strange retired officer acquires an alcohol trafficker.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum meaning strange is old-fashioned British slang; Bow Street Runners were eighteenth-century London constables.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootlegger who illegally ran liquor across borders during Prohibition was called this.

clue.text: Gave account of what the Light Brigade did

definitions.meaning: put a cost on someone's account, billed them
the Light Brigade rode headlong at the Russian guns at Balaclava in 1854

explanation.definitionFit: To bill a purchase to an account and to rush at an enemy are two meanings of the same verb.

clue.text: Given a smack by Indian cook!

definitions.text: Given a smack by Indian cook!

parts.words: Given a smack by Indian cook
parts.note: sounds like a blow from a cook, but a smack is a flavour, given by a spicy South Asian dish

explanation.definitionFit: Food flavoured with spicy sauce in the South Asian style has been seasoned this way.

clue.text: It's the most expensive, darling

definitions.meaning: highest in price, the superlative of costly
a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of costly and a fond form of address share one spelling.

clue.text: Praise firm with 1,000 employees, taking on 500 more

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
workers are men
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Applaud a business with a thousand staff that is hiring five hundred more.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend is to speak approvingly of someone, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Young Tory gets punishment in court lock up

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a fine is a monetary penalty imposed by a court

explanation.surface: A youthful Conservative is penalised by the judge and jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone is to imprison or shut them in.

clue.text: Mocked, Communist got upset and died in agony

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist

indicators.note: letters writhing in agony are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolutionary was ridiculed, became distressed and passed away in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got upset' turns RED into DER, and 'in agony' rearranges DIED into IDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule or scorn, so derided means mocked.

clue.text: Takes in the sails — in the Pacific, they're a menace

definitions.meaning: shortens sail by rolling part of it up, a sailing verb

definitions.text: in the Pacific, they're a menace
definitions.meaning: coral ridges lying just below the surface wreck ships in the Pacific

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors reduce sail area by tucking it in, and coral ridges are hazards at sea: one word for both.

clue.text: Fish king in a petty quarrel

indicators.note: the king sits inside the quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a brief, trivial argument
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A fish monarch is caught up in a small squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Station a loud-hailer in it!

parts.note: sounds like an order to set up a megaphone, but describes the voice heard over a railway station's speakers

explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads out messages over a public address system, as at a train station.

clue.text: Part of Catholic or Fundamentalist community in the Med.

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A segment of a religious congregation somewhere in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, a Mediterranean island community.

clue.text: By the look of it, how we write poetry on the page opposite

definitions.meaning: composed in lines and metre rather than prose

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the look of it' signals that the poetic phrase, written on the page as one word, also spells the word meaning opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in metre is writing in lines of poetry, while the one-word form means the reverse or contrary.

clue.text: It's not acknowledged as a sign of contempt

definitions.text: It's not acknowledged as a sign of contempt

parts.words: It's not acknowledged as a sign of contempt
parts.note: describes someone or something passed over deliberately, being snubbed to show disdain

explanation.definitionFit: To be cut dead, deliberately unnoticed, is how contempt is shown by a snub.

clue.text: Have a fling-ending up on floor, shattered!

definitions.text: Have a fling-ending up on floor, shattered!

parts.words: Have a fling-ending up on floor, shattered
parts.note: sounds like a romance ending badly, but a fling is a throw that ends with something smashed on the floor

explanation.definitionFit: To hurl something down so that it smashes on the floor is the literal sense of this phrase.
